Users using encrypted HFS+ volumes will be able to convert their volumes directly to APFS format without needing to decrypt them first, for compatibility with macOS 28. Here are the details.

Apple updates macOS 28 encrypted HFS+ volume migration guide

A few weeks ago, Apple published a support document stating that from macOS 28 onwards, Mac OS Extended will only support unencrypted volumes (disks and other storage devices).

This basically means that users currently using encrypted HFS+ external disks or other legacy Mac encrypted format volumes will need to, as Apple puts it, "decrypt or reformat all encrypted Mac OS Extended volumes."

Apple previously provided detailed steps on its support page, instructing users to either decrypt the volume or erase and reformat it as APFS.

Apple has now updated that page, adding a third option that allows users to convert encrypted HFS+ volumes directly to encrypted APFS without needing to decrypt them first. Apple has also provided instructions for this new procedure:

Converting the volume to encrypted APFS: Open Disk Utility, located in the Utilities folder within the Applications folder, or use Spotlight to search for it. From the View menu in the menu bar, select Show Only Volumes. In the sidebar of Disk Utility, select the volume's name. From the Edit menu in the menu bar, select Convert to APFS, then click Convert to confirm. Quit Disk Utility when finished.

However, Apple notes that "this option does not apply to encrypted Time Machine backup volumes."

Apple has also removed the previous instructions describing the steps to first decrypt the volume, then convert to APFS without erasing, after which re-encryption could optionally be chosen.

To view the updated support page, click here.

Will this new option help you more easily prepare your disks for upgrading to macOS 28? Let us know in the comments.
